data.bottom_line: A quick and intense storm impacted all zones last night bringing 6" of new snow to Anchorage, accompanied by strong easterly ridgetop wind. Although natural avalanches are unlikely today, there are good chances a person could trigger an avalanche up to 1.5' deep in new and windblown snow. This problem is typically found in high alpine bowls and below ridgelines, but windspeeds were strong enough to build wind slabs lower on slopes than normal. The safest thing is to give the snow some time to stabilize before getting out onto steep slopes. SUNDAY OUTLOOK: Relatively calm weather is in store Saturday and Sunday in the Front Range so the snowpack should be stabilizing. Unless ridgetop winds pick up again, it should be more difficult, on Sunday, for a person to trigger an avalanche up to 1.5' deep in windblown snow. Once wind slabs become stubborn, they may let you get way out onto a slope before releasing. Choosing slopes with clear runouts will reduce the chances of a poor outcome if you get surprised. __________________________________ SPECIAL ANNOUNCEMENTS: Forecast Operations: Chugach State Park - Weekly danger ratings on Saturday begin today. Turnagain Pass - Daily danger ratings begin today. Summit Lake - Twice per week danger ratings on Saturday and Wednesday begin this week. Seward - To be determined based on access conditions, but we will issue a product on December 1 for the motorized opener described below. On December 2nd and 3rd, the Northern Aspects Film Festival 2026 will be showing at Bear Tooth Theatrepub for its fifth year, celebrating the people, places, and stories that make skiing in Alaska unlike anywhere else. These showings will benefit the Hatcher Pass Avalanche Center and the Valdez Avalanche Center. Hope to see you there! Motorized Winter Access: Turnagain Pass opened to snowmachines on Wednesday, November 25 per the CNF Forest plan and the new over-snow vehicle use map ( OSVU map ). The remaining motorized winter riding areas on the Chugach National Forest will open December 1.
